prerequisites: Disciplinary knowledge covered by competencies ED2, ED3, ED4, ED6, ED16, acquired in previous courses of the study plan.

learning_outcomes.text: Demonstrate the ability to analyze and synthesize.
Acquire the ability to effectively solve problems.
Express oneself correctly in Spanish, both orally and in writing.
Possess knowledge of Information and Communication Technologies (ICT).
Acquire skills related to the use of computer programs for calculation, data analysis and processing within their field of application.
Develop the ability to transmit information, ideas, problems and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Develop the ability to search for and manage information.
Develop critical reasoning.
Develop interpersonal skills.
Develop the ability to work in a team.
Acquire commitment to ethics and social responsibility.
Develop the ability to put acquired knowledge into practice.
Acquire the ability for autonomous learning and concern for knowledge and continuous training.
Develop the ability to adapt to new situations.
Develop the ability to generate new ideas (creativity).
Be able to work autonomously.
Become aware of issues related to the environment.
Understanding and mastery of quality management, environmental management and occupational risk prevention.
Knowledge and capabilities for the application of energy saving and efficiency systems in mechanical machines and installations.
Knowledge about technological, mechanical, electrical, energy and electronic applications.
Ability for Quality, Safety and Environmental Management.
Ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Understand the basic concepts of Environmental Science and Sustainability.
Know the dynamics of pollutants in aquatic systems and the main water treatment processes (potabilization and purification).
Know the dynamics of atmospheric pollutants and the processes for treating gaseous effluents.
Know the classification of different types of waste and the specific procedures for their environmental management.
Know the problem of contaminated soils and the main treatment techniques for them.
Understand renewable energies as a family of technologies compatible with environmental preservation.
Know the most common renewable resources and their main utilization technologies.
Know the basic procedures for sizing solar, wind, etc. installations.
Train in the handling of specific instruments and software related to renewable energies.
Know the basic regulatory framework applicable to renewable energy installations.

syllabus_topics: Composition and quality parameters of natural waters.
Main pollutants to be removed in water potabilization.
Legislation on discharges: the discharge fee.
Tema 3 - Control/Tratamiento de la contaminación atmosférica
Main atmospheric pollutants and emission sources.
Air quality criteria: emission and immission.
Dispersion of pollutants in the atmosphere.
Purification of atmospheric pollutants: gaseous pollutant purification and particle purification.
Control of pollutants in stationary sources.
Contamination from energy sources: electromagnetic radiation.
Treatments: non-hazardous waste landfill, incineration, composting, recycling.
Treatment: physical-chemical treatments, incineration, hazardous waste landfill.
Tema 6 - Contaminación del suelo y técnicas de tratamiento
Treatment techniques: thermal technologies, physical-chemical technologies, biological technologies.
Las Energías Renovables y la preservación del Medio Ambiente
Energy outlook in Spain and worldwide.
Movement of the Sun in the celestial sphere.
Very low temperature technologies: heat pump.

assessment_methods.method: Renewable Energies - Instrumental laboratory practical assessment.
Environment - Theoretical knowledge assessment: continuous assessment tests at the end of each topic.
Environment - Instrumental laboratory practical assessment (mandatory attendance): assessment test at the end of practices.

assessment_rules: To pass, a minimum of 5/10 is required in the weighted average for both the 'Renewable Energies' and 'Environment' sections, with the overall grade being the average of these two. Specific components have minimum passing grades ranging from 2.5/10 to 4.0/10. Most components are recoverable in the 2nd examination period, except for instrumental laboratory practices which require mandatory attendance and cannot be recovered if missed. Exceptional evaluation is available for students completing at least 40% of lab sessions, involving an oral test (30%), a written test (20%), a project defense (30%), and lab session evaluation (20%), each requiring a minimum of 3/10 and a weighted average of 5/10.
